short: Context prior from the decoded question (M07) is ahead, gaining in 3 of 3 participants; HMM decoder (M06) is standard; the real-time claim rests on offline simulation only.
position: The paper changes two components. Its use-time context (M07), a soft prior over the 24 answers from the decoded likelihoods of the perceived question, is ahead: no earlier study among 36 dialogue-context matches in 1,280 brain-signal decoding studies (pattern match) used such a prior, the deciding priors constrain output only with a fixed sentence set or an n-gram model (Moses et al. 2018; Herff et al. 2015), and the gain is significant in each of three participants. Its decoder (M06), neural speech-event detection plus phone-HMM Viterbi scoring of each candidate utterance, is standard, extending the group's perception decoders to produced speech. The real-time claim outruns the evidence: every accuracy is an offline simulation and the bedside runs report no accuracy figure. The context gain is a closed-set grammar effect (answers outside the decoded question's set get zero prior), and a hard or true-question prior helped little, so it says nothing yet about open conversation.
